Price of one currency in another

walkthroughs.body_html:
Each country usually has a currency.

  • UK — pound sterling (£).
  • USA — dollar ($).
  • Eurozone — euro (€).
  • Japan — yen (¥).

The exchange rate tells you how much one currency is worth in another.

£1 = $1.25 → £100 swaps to $125.

Rates change every day.

A strong pound buys more abroad — cheaper holidays for Brits.

A weak pound makes imports pricier but UK exports cheaper for foreigners.

So it's good for some, bad for others. ✈️

mcqs.q: Why do economists generally argue against protectionism?
options: Opportunity cost is the money price of something.
Protectionism means protecting national parks from development.

Tariffs and quotas raise prices for consumers, protect inefficient industries, invite retaliation, and reduce overall welfare — even when they save specific jobs, the cost per job saved typically exceeds the wage.
Protectionism always makes a country richer by keeping money at home.
